newsitem.title: USA: Morgan Stanley, Dean Witter plan may boost ratings.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley, Dean Witter plan may boost ratings.

text.p: The proposed merger of Wall Street powerhouses Dean Witter, Discover & Co and Morgan Stanley Group Inc met favorable review by two top international credit rating agencies on Wednesday.
In all, about $20 billion in outstanding debt is affected, according to Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's.

The ratings of both Morgan Stanley and lower-rated Dean Witter were placed on review for upgrade by Moody's, with the agency citing potential for enhanced profits for what would be the largest investment banking concern in the world.
Moody's said it may raise the A2 and A1 long-term debt ratings of Dean Witter and Morgan Stanley, respectively.

"There is the possibility for franchise benefits deriving from the fact that you can now link a very solid investment banking franchise with an extensive retail distribution network," said Haig Nargesian, senior analyst with Moody's Financial Institutions Group.
The greatest challenge, Nargesian said, is that the two firms are distinctly different businesses that now must work together. But one positive, he said, is there is not much overlap between the two.

Standard & Poor's also said it may upgrade Dean Witter's long-term debt rating, currently single-A, based on "positive business implications." In its release, S&P said the end product will be "a premier franchise in both retail and institutional securities services, with complementary origination and distribution capabilities."
Like Moody's, S&P also noted the companies face an enormous task of melding businesses. This concern, in fact, led to only a ratings affirmation of Morgan Stanley's A-plus long-term rating by S&P.

S&P said it puts "significant weight" on both management teams to execute stratgies, and "clashes of corporate culture are a risk whenever two distinct financial institutions merge." But S&P couched its comment, saying it believes both companies have the management depth to meet the challenge.
Moody's Nargesian said the review, depending on the completion of the merger, would probably close within a six-month time frame.
Charles Rauch, director of S&P's financial institutions group, also said the review is dependent on the merger's success and completion.
He would not say if Morgan Stanley's long-term rating would be considered for an upgrade later.

"There is a positive for Morgan Stanley but the key to a further upgrade down the road will depend on how successful they are in getting the two companies and their businesses to work together," said Rauch, adding that "You don't want to jam the two together."
There is one possible black spot, however, said S&P.

It may lower Morgan Stanley's A-1-plus short-term rating, noting that funding strategies must be revamped to accommodate the $33 billion of "less-liquid" on- and off-balance sheet credit card receivables of Dean Witter.

Morgan Stanley and Dean Witter on Wednesday announced they reached a definitive agreement to merge, creating an industry giant with a combined market capitalization of $21 billion. The new entity would be called Morgan Stanley, Dean Witter, Discover & Co.
